question: Wires of copper, silver, nichrome and glass are made having similar length and diameter. Which will have the highest resistance?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Glass__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __**Key Points**__

__
 
• **Resistance**

 
 
• **​**Electrical resistance, denoted by R, occurs when an **electric current **passes through a conductor, such as a light bulb. This obstruction is known as **electrical resistance.**
 
• Conductors **generate heat** when current passes through them because every material has electrical resistance.
 
• There is a relationship between the **potential difference** across a conductor and the **current** that flows through it, according to** Ohm's law**. It comes from,
 
 
• **V ∝ I V = IR**
 
• Where** V** is the potential difference measured across the conductor in** volts,**
 
• **'I'** is the conductor's current in **amperes**, and
 
• **'R'** is the resistance constant in **ohms.**​**​**
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Electrical Resistance**

 
 
• **​**The **cross-sectional area **of the conductor
 
• **Length** of the conductor
 
• The** material **of the conductor
 
• The **temperature** of the conducting material
 
 
• Electrical resistance is **inversely proportional** to the conductor's **cross-sectional area (A)** and **directly proportional to its length (L)**. The relationship that follows provides it.
 
• **R= ρL/A**
 
• where** ρ** is the **resistivity** of the material (measured in Ωm, ohm meter).
